content.title: THE DAILY MINIMUMS YOUR {{BODY}} IS QUIETLY BEGGING FOR
facts: **Sunlight** -> 15 min before 10am -> Locks in circadian clock
**Walking** -> 20 min after dinner -> Flattens blood sugar spike
**Cold water** -> 500 ml right after waking -> Kickstarts alertness
**Deep breathing** -> 5 min, slow exhales -> Drops stress hormones
**Silence** -> 10 min, no screens -> Resets mental fatigue
**Stretching** -> 5 min before bed -> Deepens sleep quality
**Gratitude** -> 1 sentence written daily -> Lowers anxious thoughts
**Sleep** -> 7-9 hours, consistent time -> Repairs muscle and mood
**Follow along** -> for more daily health tips like this -> Simple habits, real results
content.caption:
A few of these daily minimums deserve a deeper look. Sunlight exposure in the morning hits receptors in your eyes that tell your brain to suppress melatonin and set your internal clock for the next 16 hours - skip it, and your whole sleep-wake rhythm drifts later. Walking after dinner works because contracting leg muscles pull glucose out of your bloodstream without needing extra insulin, which is why a short post-meal walk blunts the sugar spike so effectively. And that 25-30g of protein at breakfast slows gastric emptying and stabilizes ghrelin, the hormone that triggers hunger, so you're not white-knuckling it until lunch. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so treat these as a starting baseline, not a strict rulebook.
